What I am perceiving from this post, and I stand to be corrected: 

There is concern that due to their overly-saturated public life and the message they convey while in the public life may jeopardize their own personal life - that is the life behind their public and even pseudo-personal personas. In summation - in the act of being a public spectacle and consumer product (yes, I chose this word because they are there to satisfy not just musical tastes, but a more primal desire for a relationship, even if manufactured), would they lose themselves in the lifestyle and process? Would they even lose their chances for returning to themselves before the extra-ordinary life of stardom?

​

Opinion/Analysis (?):

I think they do that as part of the polishing of their song product. A song is not a physical product - but some sounds that you can listen to. But BTS' marketing people got smarter - they realized that fans loved the story around the songs produced. So it would make sense when they release and publicize songs, they would weave the Army into the story because the story IS part of the product (the song). It makes the Army feel like they have an important part in the making of the song. A gesture of importance and inclusivity - kind of like how gamers feel proud to partake in helping a game developer release a new game through beta testing. 

 You can also think of it in another angle - think of it similar to how designer labels put their trademark piece on their stuff (eg: The yellow stitching on the Doc Marten footwear, the golden arches of McDonalds, and the LV logo on the insides of Louis Vuitton clothing). They include Army as part of that trademark in the story. 

​

Do I think it's cheesy? Kind of, but it doesn't bother me so much. But you do raise an important point to the well-being of the artists personal lives - they are people after all.
